html:
Compiled setup primitives and scoped directory repair

Compiled distributions use standard-library helpers before the normal application runtime is available. This page explains common.py, interaction.py and permissions.py: paths, verified input bytes, local receipts, locking, invocation consent/output and narrowly scoped directory repair. The bootstrap package links the installation, update, service and removal owners that use these primitives. Those complete workflows are not implemented by these three helpers. The compiled launch and dependency flow follows these primitives through managed generations, platform prerequisites and application entry.

Invocation state and command output

The compiled entry point opens an interaction.session with explicit invocation options. Its ContextVar holds approval, verbosity, noninteractive intent and configured legal options. Nested sessions restore their outer state on exit, including failure; there is no environment-variable switch in this helper that grants installation approval.

sequenceDiagram participant Owner as Compiled setup owner participant Session as Invocation context participant Legal as Bundled installation-acceptance owner participant Process as Selected subprocess participant Output as Terminal / private diagnostic log Owner->>Session: Open session and configure component/version acceptance options Session->>Legal: Validate flags and bundled document identity opt Reusing native installer approval Session->>Session: Require matching document versions and content hashes end Owner->>Session: Confirm before setup work alt Session already approved Session-->>Owner: Reuse this invocation approval else Approval needed Session->>Legal: Obtain explicit versioned or terminal acceptance Legal-->>Session: Acceptance receipt or failure Session-->>Owner: Mark approved only after success end Note over Owner,Process: The caller owns command selection and consent ordering Owner->>Session: Run selected argv with environment, directory and timeout alt Ordinary or verbose output Session->>Process: Execute with stderr progress or requested capture else Quiet setup output opt sudo authentication is not already noninteractive Session->>Output: Authenticate visibly before quiet command end Session->>Process: Execute with private diagnostics and optional stdout capture end Process-->>Session: Result or OS/subprocess failure opt Quiet diagnostic log was created Session->>Output: Remove successful log or retain failed-command log end Session-->>Owner: Captured stdout or propagated failure Owner->>Session: Exit and restore outer invocation context

configure_legal checks explicit flags and binds component/product-version options. If approval came through the native installer handoff, it checks the current bundled document versions and content hashes against that handoff. confirm reuses an already approved session; otherwise it requires configured legal context, prints the data root and calls the shared installation acceptance owner. That owner handles the actual prompts/flags and receipt. These functions describe installer behavior; they do not modify the bundled terms or product clickwrap state.

The dependency installer's ensure_environment rejects running the application as an administrator. A ready ordinary environment can be returned before new setup is needed. When setup is needed, it confirms acceptance before entering the directory repair scope. Custom-runtime and later dependency publication decisions belong to installer.py.

interaction.run executes an argument list without a shell and propagates checked subprocess failures. It does not call confirm itself. Outside a session, or in verbose mode, output goes to stderr unless capture was requested. In quiet mode, diagnostics go to a private temporary log; successful logs are removed, while OSError and subprocess failures retain the log and print its path. Captured stdout remains available to machine callers. A quiet sudo command without -n first runs visible authentication, then uses -n for the command, so its password prompt is not hidden in the log. The caller controls whether such a command is appropriate for the invocation's noninteractive policy.

Paths, integrity and publication

data_root returns SMTO_COMPILED_HOME only when that explicit override is absolute. Otherwise it uses the platform's SMTO application-data location. cache_root has a separate platform cache location; changing the compiled data root does not redirect downloads. Both functions return paths without creating them. The private_directory operation checks for symlink components, creates the final directory and enforces current-user ownership and mode 0700 on POSIX. Windows does not run that POSIX ownership/mode branch.

interpreter searches the expected virtual-environment and embedded-runtime paths. If none exists, it returns the preferred candidate for its caller to diagnose. Finding a path is not an ABI check or proof that the executable works.

flowchart TD Spec[Caller-supplied URL and SHA-256 pin] --> Validate[Require HTTPS URL and<br/>64 lowercase hexadecimal digest] Validate --> Cache[Open private download cache] Cache --> Hit{Nonsymlink cached file<br/>has expected digest?} Hit -->|Yes| Return[Return verified file path] Hit -->|No| Offline{Offline mode?} Offline -->|Yes| Missing[Fail with missing pinned input] Offline -->|No| Temp[Create sibling temporary download] Temp --> Fetch[HTTPS request using default TLS context<br/>and 60-second request timeout] Fetch --> Verify[Require HTTPS final URL<br/>and expected byte digest] Verify --> Publish[Replace digest-named cache entry] Publish --> Return Fetch -->|OS or timeout failure| Retry{Attempts remain?} Verify -->|OS read failure| Retry Publish -->|OS failure| Retry Retry -->|Yes| Backoff[Wait 1 then 2 seconds<br/>Remove temporary file before retry] Backoff --> Temp Retry -->|No| Fail[Remove temporary file and propagate failure] Verify -->|Redirect or digest rejection| Fail Return --> Extract[Caller may extract into its staging directory]

download verifies bytes against the supplied pin; the caller still owns the provenance of that pin. Cache hits are checked again, including in offline mode. Online transfers use a temporary file, validate the final redirect scheme and hash, then replace the digest-named entry. There are at most three attempts for OS/timeout errors. Redirect or digest validation errors are immediate failures. The timeout is passed to each request; it is not one deadline covering every retry and setup operation. Temporary download names are removed on all these exits.

ZIP extraction checks every member name before extraction, rejecting absolute paths, parent traversal, backslashes, colons and symlink entries. TAR extraction delegates to Python's data filter. Extraction is not atomic and can leave partial output after an I/O failure, so the staging owner must decide cleanup/publication. Verified input bytes do not imply that every subsequent setup operation succeeded.

digest hashes file bytes, while identity hashes compact sorted-key JSON values. write_json writes indented JSON to a sibling temporary file and replaces the final receipt path. Replacement prevents readers seeing a partially written JSON file; this helper does not fsync a durable checkpoint or provide a transaction across several receipts/files.

installation_lock uses a regular, single-link file in a private directory. POSIX uses flock; Windows locks one initialized byte. Contention retries every two seconds until the monotonic deadline, which defaults to one hour. The context manager unlocks and closes on exit, and process termination releases the OS lock. The file can remain for reuse; a stale PID file is not its ownership mechanism. Optional wait messages follow the current verbosity policy.

Scoped POSIX directory repair

%%{init: {'flowchart': {'rankSpacing': 25, 'nodeSpacing': 25}}}%% flowchart TD Bad[Directory ownership/mode needs repair] --> Scope{Repair enabled?} Scope -->|No| Refuse[Stop with error] Scope -->|Yes| Owned{Owned by caller?} Owned -->|Yes| Chmod[Try chmod 0700 on this directory] Chmod -->|Success| Verify[Recheck path links, device/inode,<br/>directory type, owner and mode] Chmod -->|Permission denied| Interactive{Interactive policy<br/>and terminal?} Owned -->|No| Interactive Interactive -->|No| Refuse Interactive -->|Yes| Sudo{sudo available<br/>and approved?} Sudo -->|No| Refuse Sudo -->|Yes| Helper[Run fixed helper with isolated private Python] Helper --> Walk[Open each path component without following links] Walk --> Same{Same device/inode?} Same -->|No| Refuse Same -->|Yes| Repair[Change only final directory owner and mode] Repair --> Verify Verify --> Match{Postchecks pass?} Match -->|Yes| Return[Return repaired private directory] Match -->|No| Refuse

directory_repairs enables repair only for its dynamic scope and restores the previous policy afterward. An enabled noninteractive scope can still fix mode bits on a directory already owned by the current user. Elevation requires interactive input, sudo availability and a separate affirmative response. Decline, EOF or interruption stops repair. The helper does not read or retain the sudo password.

For elevation, the fixed _REPAIR program runs with the launcher's Python in isolated/no-site mode. It opens path components without following links and checks the original device/inode before changing the final directory. It changes that directory's owner/group and mode, not its contents or parents. Both ordinary chmod and elevated repair then run verify_directory; an exit code alone is insufficient. These are distinct checks and operations, not a recursive repair or a single transaction over the installation tree.

Verification boundaries

The selected primitive tests cover path override validation, symlink rejection, offline pinned-cache corruption, archive traversal and cross-process lock contention. The interaction tests cover invocation-local acceptance, output modes, captured results and retained failure logs. Permission tests use temporary directories and simulated sudo, including changed inode/link rejection and failed post-repair verification. All 36 selected cases pass. Helper subprocesses run only inside these fixtures; no dependency installation, live download, system package operation or real privilege escalation is performed by this documentation review.

Full Python AST comparison preserves the embedded repair program, legal/command strings and all executable behavior. The review covers these shared primitives and stated caller boundaries, not a full platform release or installer acceptance campaign. Existing build instructions remain the entry point for producing distributions.
